summary: Elevated 5xx rate after graceful-drain delay on API gateway causing upstream overload
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 02:05 UTC we observed a sustained uptick in 5xx responses for a small set of dedicated tenants (notably Acadia Analytics) served from us-east-1. Error mix was 502/503/504 and error rate rose from baseline ~0.2% to ~7% over a 15 minute window. Impact: Customer requests failing (chat completions and short streaming sessions) and visible errors in their product. Some long-lived sessions disconnected. This appears to correlate with a scheduled node maintenance window in the same AZ where graceful-drain timing was modified earlier in the day. Environment: prod - us-east-1, Dedicated pool pool-az1, API gateway cluster apigw-prod-us-east-1, runtime fleet running redwood/fastgen-2.1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a maintenance drain on a subset of apigw nodes with an extended 'linger' delay setting (simulate delayed connection close)
2) Simulate sustained tenant traffic to dedicated pool (concurrent short streaming + generate requests at 200 rps from single client)
3) Observe API gateway accepting new connections while upstream runtime drains slowly; watch queue growth on upstream proxies
4) Trigger small scale pod restarts on runtime nodes to observe probe interactions and any autoscaler churn
logs: 2026-03-12T02:07:11Z apigw[proxy-12] WARN conn: accepted socket but upstream busy -> queue=312 backlog=512
2026-03-12T02:07:18Z apigw[proxy-12] ERROR response: upstream reset (502) tenant=acadia-01 request_id=abc123
2026-03-12T02:09:02Z runtime[node-7] WARN probe: liveness failed 3/3 -> restarting pod
2026-03-12T02:09:04Z autoscaler INFO scale: attempted scale up 2 -> 4 but blocked by cpuQuota, scale failed
2026-03-12T02:11:30Z apigw[proxy-12] ERROR response: queue full -> 503 tenant=acadia-01 request_id=def456
2026-03-12T02:12:20Z apigw[proxy-12] ERROR response: gateway timeout waiting for upstream -> 504
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: delayed drain setting kept acceptor sockets open while upstream nodes were removed, causing connection handoff to overloaded upstreams and queue backlog in the apigw proxy.
Observed multiple runtime restarts triggered by liveness failures during the same window; restart churn amplified load (rebuilding KV prefetched shards and reloading models).
Autoscaler attempted to add capacity but was blocked on tenant-level CPU quota enforcement in the dedicated pool (quota misalignment).
Health-check aggression: readiness probe timeout configured at 5s; with increased queueing readiness flapped causing more pod restarts.
We saw large numbers of keepalive sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on the apigw nodes during the window (socket linger setting was 60s).
mitigation_steps: 1) Immediate rollback: Reverted earlier graceful-drain 'linger' change to previous 5s on apigw nodes (rolled back at 2026-03-12T03:00 UTC)
2) Temporarily raised per-tenant connection limit and enabled emergency rate-shed for noisy tenants to prevent queue exhaustion
3) Increased autoscaler quota check path to allow transient burst scaling while we stabilize (short-term exception granted to dedicated pool)
4) Adjusted readiness probe window from 5s -> 10s for runtime pods to reduce flapping during backlog recovery
resolution: Short-term: rollback of drain linger + temporary autoscaler quota exception and probe tuning reduced 5xx rate back to baseline by 2026-03-12T03:40 UTC. Customer (Acadia Analytics) confirmed degraded behavior resolved for live traffic. Long-term: engineering will land a fix that hardens apigw backpressure handling (non-blocking accept/shard queues), add tenant-priority fair-queueing, and introduce a pre-drain handshake so upstreams can finish inflight requests before node removal. Patch PR created (#4521).
next_steps: Schedule CR for apigw backpressure patch and pre-drain handshake (owner: SRE team)
Follow up with Capacity/Quota team to reconcile dedicated pool burst allowances for scheduled maintenance windows
Add automated test to maintenance window runbook to simulate drain timing and measure 5xx impact
Notify customers on dedicated tier of outgoing change that increases robustness during future drains
